summary: Normative R2 selects and substantially resolves all four original data mechanisms: typed purpose links, session-first locks, durable epochs and activation, precise deadlines, and retained bounded tombstones. Two narrow local corrections remain: a full ownership reply cannot fit the 8,192-byte progress cap for a supported 100-step Session, and the NOT_INVOKED matrix uses an unsupported FAILED/CANCELLED report tuple. Both are prose-level corrections independent of provider facts.

findings.category: Ownership claim replay-cache bound versus supported Session size
findings.finding: R2 selects OwnershipGrant1 containing the whole unchanged Session and persists last number/request hash/reply to reproduce an original duplicate acknowledgment. Its combined epoch/claim/control progress bound is8192bytes. A supported100-step Session alone exceeds that bound; the selected full-reply cache has no concrete compact representation. Thus a literal implementation either rejects otherwise supported ownership, exceeds its storage cap, or reconstructs a different duplicate reply/lease. This is locally resolvable and independent of provider facts.

staticByteAnalysis.method: Read-only canonical JSON size calculation based on the existing v2 fixture Session, replacing only sourceSteps with100 unique UUIDs and setting existing maxSourceSteps100. No validator/test/browser/DB was executed; this is a serialization counterexample, not integration evidence.
staticByteAnalysis.scope: Does not claim every field combination or complete100-step workflow is executable; demonstrates the unchanged supported Session response shape cannot fit the stated full-reply cache.

findings.requiredCorrection: Select a bounded compact ownership-cache projection and exact reply reconstruction algorithm: retain every mutable field required to reproduce the accepted original grant (including its original lease/fence/state/counters/account-connection snapshot/dbTime as applicable), use verified immutable parent facts for the large source/scope/version parts, and define stale/terminal/fence behavior without extending lease or dropping mode. Alternatively select a separately justified finite full-response cache bound covering the actual supported Session maximum, adjust aggregate quotas accordingly, and preserve old limits. Do not lower supported source-step count, truncate fields, return current renewed lease on an old duplicate, or infer legacy mode to fit the cap. Specify the selected cache in normative prose rather than leaving this concrete layout choice to implementation.

Move action/counters/state and renew lease after an acknowledgment, then replay the prior renewal counter/body: receive its original grant/deadline semantics without extending rights; changed/old/skipped counter or changed fence cannot recreate accepting authority.

findings.category: Outcome pair incompatible with existing report verifier
findings.overlap: Root relayed the security peer finding under this ID; independently confirmed against the actual unchanged GuidedActionLedger.verifyReport source.
findings.finding: The new matrix specifies authenticated NOT_INVOKED after consumed intent as FAILED/dispatchCount1 with outcomeCode TIMEOUT or CANCELLED. verifyReport permits FAILED only with ASSERTION_FAILED, TARGET_CHANGED, POLICY_DENIED or TIMEOUT; CANCELLED is not a valid FAILED owning-worker report. Merely being present in the wider ledger enum does not grant this tuple. The statement that only existing supported ledger codes are used is therefore not satisfied.
findings.requiredCorrection: Select an actually supported existing FAILED tuple for known NOT_INVOKED authority cancellation/expiry, while retaining the precise cancellation/expiry cause in the authority wrapper and session terminal state. Preserve dispatchCount1 as consumed intent. If a terminal cancellation/UNKNOWN/fence change already won, only append the bounded historical receipt and keep existing action/session state. Do not reset to REVOKED/count0, expand the frozen legacy verifier or bypass it merely to implement this prose.
